title: Rabbi Chiyya of Vastanya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Taanit 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9a.14) relates that he, Rav Shmuel bar Idi and Rav Huna bar Manoach used to be before Rava. When Rava died, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a teaching that did not seem reasonable to them, they would signal to one another. Rav Papa was distressed, and [in a dream he was made to read](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b.1): “And I cut off the three shepherds.” The next day, when they took leave of him, he said to them, “Let the Rabbis go in peace.” Yuchasin wrote that they died. Hyman observes that the Gemara does not say that the dream was fulfilled. In [Zevachim 112a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.112a.9): “Rabbi Chiyya of Yustinya said: With a Nasi’s goat”; Dikdukei Soferim reads of Vastinya, and it is a place-name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Taanit identifies Rava as the teacher who died and Rav Papa as the teacher who dreamed. The Bavli records the farewell without saying that the three died.
The consulted Bavli calls him Rav Chiyya. Taanit has Vostanya and the farewell bishlama. Zevachim has Yustinya and speaks of a ruler’s goat. Hyman reports the Dikdukei Soferim form Vastinya.
